Two concurrent invocations in the same workspace were explicitly disallowed for this window by the binding rules and are recorded as undone. Per gaps [3] and [12]'s next_check.
preregistered: Foreground: if `claude -p '/codex:review --wait --scope branch --base <sha> --json'` exits 0 and returns a JSON envelope with a real codex.stdout review body, that reconfirms the prior foreground result from foundation-rd-20260921 on a fresh diff and settles the foreground portion of gap [12]. Background: `claude -p '/codex:review --background ...'` is expected to return a job id promptly; this check then polls that job via `/codex:status` and `/codex:result` within the unit's remaining claude -p budget (at most two further calls) and records whatever terminal or non-terminal state is observed at that point, without retrying to obtain a different outcome. A terminal status (completed or failed) with a readable result would newly qualify background polling behaviour for gap [3] as working end to end. A job that has not reached a terminal state within the polling budget -- whether because the underlying worker process is still running, has exited without updating job state, or any other cause -- is recorded as-is as a genuine partial/inconclusive result for background reliability within this budget, not as a failure to be retried past the budget. Same-workspace concurrency remains explicitly out of scope for this window (binding rules) and is recorded as undone, consistent with foundation-rd-20260921's 'concurrency remain unqualified' limitation, which this receipt does not close.

verdict_impact.explanation: Foreground /codex:review is reconfirmed working end to end and matches the prior foundation-rd-20260921 result, so it supports the incumbent lane as a review tool. Background mode, however, produced a genuinely stuck job (worker process exited but the job's own state file was never updated past 'running', and /codex:result returned nothing) -- this is a new, reproducible operational finding, not a retry-to-fix result. It does not by itself argue for replacing the lane (no alternative was compared), but it means gap [3]'s 'background polling behaviour ... unqualified' is now qualified as unreliable in this one observed run, and should not be treated as a settled-working capability without further investigation (e.g. whether this is a one-off orphan or a reproducible defect in the plugin's background job supervisor).

limitations: Model, effort and token usage for both the foreground and background Codex reviews were not recoverable: the companion envelope omits them, the workspace-keyed plugin job ledger for the --wait invocation showed an empty jobs[] array (apparently not persisted for --wait mode), and no matching Codex thread/session record was found in ~/.codex/sqlite/thread_history_1.sqlite or ~/.codex/sessions/ for either threadId. This matches, and does not newly resolve, foundation-rd-20260921.json's existing 'usage/model/effort are not exposed' limitation.

The background job's stuck state was observed once, in one run, on one small diff; whether it reproduces on a larger diff, a different workspace, or a later plugin version is not established here. No root-cause investigation (e.g. reading the plugin's own source or the job's session logs beyond the 4 lines captured) was performed within this unit's scope and model-call budget.
The two-concurrent-invocations sub-check named in gap [3]'s next_check was not attempted this window per the binding rules and is recorded as undone below, not as a negative result.

claude -p model-call budget for this unit (at most 4, each driving one Codex review) was fully used by the two review invocations plus the two polling calls (/codex:status, /codex:result) needed to observe the background job's terminal (non-)state; no further polling or a /codex:cancel call was made once the budget was exhausted, so the background job's plugin-side ledger may still show 'running' after this receipt is written.

The scratch multi-file diff (3 small files, one deliberate synthetic bug) is a fixture, not a representative production diff; reviewer quality/coverage on larger or more realistic changes is not assessed here.
